chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If a camel resists you while you intend to slaughter it, and it gets away from you, and you fear it will escape before you, so you strike it with a sword or thrust it with a spear after reciting the name of God, then eat it, unless you catch it and it has not yet died, in which case you slaughter it properly."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an animal escapes during slaughter in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the procedural nuances of *dhabh* (slaughter) when an animal resists, permitting the use of weapons like swords or spears provided *Tasmiyah* (mentioning God's name) is recited prior to the strike. It establishes a practical legal distinction between killing the animal in the field versus catching it alive, where the latter requires the standard ritual slaughter to ensure the meat is *Halal*. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the validity of the name of God even in dynamic, non-traditional slaughter scenarios.
